results.title: Eigenvalues of −A, strict subspace tests and eigenvalue counts
aliases: positivity on a subspace counts eigenvalues
results.informal: For symmetric $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ with decreasing eigenvalues $\lambda_0\ge\dots\ge\lambda_{n-1}$ (`eigenvalues₀`): $\lambda_k(-A)=-\lambda_{n-1-k}(A)$. If $x^\top Ax>c\|x\|^2$ for all nonzero $x$ in a subspace of dimension $k+1$, then $\lambda_k(A)>c$ (strict form of the existing non-strict test); consequently a $k$-dimensional subspace on which $x^\top Ax\ge0$ (resp. $>0$ off $0$) forces at least $k$ nonnegative (resp. positive) eigenvalues.
hypotheses: strict test: $x^\top Ax>c\,x^\top x$ for all $x\in S\setminus\{0\}$
results.notes: Bookkeeping lemmas that let every upper Weyl/Courant–Fischer bound be turned into the matching lower bound by negation (Thm 4.3.1 (4.3.2b), Cor 4.3.15 lower half), and the strict variant needed for strict interlacing and inertia arguments (`sylvester-inertia`). Prove (routine from the existing variational lemmas `le_eigenvalues₀_of_forall_mem`, `eigenvalues₀_le_of_forall_mem`; strictness via compactness of the unit sphere).

results.title: Interlacing for low-rank and definite updates of a symmetric matrix
results.informal: Let $A,B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric (increasing order $\lambda_1\le\dots\le\lambda_n$). If $B$ has $\pi$ positive and $\nu$ negative eigenvalues then $\lambda_i(A+B)\le\lambda_{i+\pi}(A)$ and $\lambda_{i-\nu}(A)\le\lambda_i(A+B)$. In particular if $\operatorname{rank}B=r$ then $\lambda_{i-r}(A)\le\lambda_i(A+B)\le\lambda_{i+r}(A)$, and for $z\in\mathbb R^n$: $\lambda_i(A)\le\lambda_i(A+zz^\top)\le\lambda_{i+1}(A)$ and $\lambda_{i-1}(A)\le\lambda_i(A-zz^\top)\le\lambda_i(A)$.
results.notes: Consumers: Nyström and low-rank-plus-residual analyses ($A-\hat A$ has rank $\le n-k$ perturbation structure), `partial-cholesky-nystrom` (each pivot step is a rank-one downdate), deflation in `subspace-iteration-convergence`, and eigenvalue counting in `sylvester-inertia`. Prove: each statement is `eigenvalues₀_add_le` with the $j$ index set to the number of nonzero eigenvalues of $B$ (whose $j$-th sorted eigenvalue is then $\le0$).

results.title: Converse of interlacing: bordered and rank-one realisations
aliases: inverse eigenvalue problem for bordered matrices
results.informal: If real numbers satisfy $\mu_1\le\lambda_1\le\mu_2\le\dots\le\lambda_n\le\mu_{n+1}$, there are $a\in\mathbb R$ and $y\in\mathbb R^n$ such that $\begin{bmatrix}\Lambda&y\\y^\top&a\end{bmatrix}$ with $\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda)$ has eigenvalues $\mu_1,\dots,\mu_{n+1}$. If $\lambda_1\le\mu_1\le\lambda_2\le\dots\le\lambda_n\le\mu_n$, there is $z\in\mathbb R^n$ with $\operatorname{spec}(\Lambda+zz^\top)=\{\mu_i\}$.
results.conclusion: existence of $a,y$ (resp. $z$) realising the prescribed spectrum

mathlib_prereqs.note: Matrix determinant lemma for the rank-one case.

results.notes: Consumers: constructing Jacobi matrices with prescribed Ritz values (lower-bound instances for Lanczos/`kaniel-paige-saad`, `jacobi-matrix-identities`). Assume is acceptable; proof via the secular equation.

results.title: Eigenvalues of the Hermitian part majorize the real parts of the eigenvalues
results.informal: For $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ with eigenvalues $z_i$ and Hermitian part $H(A)=(A+A^*)/2$, the vector $\lambda(H(A))$ majorizes $(\operatorname{Re}z_i)$; conversely every such pair $x\succ\operatorname{Re}z$ is realised by some $A$. Corollary (Bendixson): $\lambda_{\min}(H(A))\le\operatorname{Re}z_i\le\lambda_{\max}(H(A))$.
results.notes: Consumers: `field-of-values-def` (Re W(A) = [λmin(H), λmax(H)]), `gmres-elman` (positive-real matrices have Re λ > 0). Prove the forward direction via Schur triangularisation + Schur (Thm 4.3.45); the converse may be assumed.

results.title: Haynsworth inertia additivity of the Schur complement
results.informal: For symmetric $M=\begin{bmatrix}A&B\\B^\top&C\end{bmatrix}$ with $A$ invertible and $S=C-B^\top A^{-1}B$: $i_+(M)=i_+(A)+i_+(S)$, $i_-(M)=i_-(A)+i_-(S)$, $i_0(M)=i_0(S)$. In particular $M\succ0$ iff $A\succ0$ and $S\succ0$.

mathlib_prereqs.note: Sylvester uniqueness used for the congruence $M\cong A\oplus S$.

results.notes: Consumers: block LDLᵀ inertia counts (generalises the scalar-pivot `card_eigenvalues_lt_eq_card_neg_of_eq_mul_diagonal_mul` in `sylvester-inertia`), saddle-point/KKT systems, `partial-cholesky-nystrom`. Prove from the block congruence $M=L(A\oplus S)L^\top$ and `inertiaPos_transpose_mul_mul`.

results.title: Ostrowski's theorem: eigenvalues under congruence
results.informal: For symmetric $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ and $S\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ with singular values $\sigma_1\ge\dots\ge\sigma_n$, for each $k$ there is $\theta_k\in[\sigma_n^2,\sigma_1^2]$ with $\lambda_k(SAS^\top)=\theta_k\lambda_k(A)$ (same ordering). Hence $\sigma_n^2\lambda_k(A)\le\lambda_k(SAS^\top)\le\sigma_1^2\lambda_k(A)$ for $\lambda_k(A)\ge0$ (reversed for $\lambda_k(A)<0$), and $SAS^\top$ has no more positive (negative) eigenvalues than $A$.
results.notes: Consumers: eigenvalues of preconditioned or sketched Gram matrices $S A S^\top$ (`sketch-and-precondition`, `preconditioned-cg`, `nystrom-pcg`), quantitative inertia. Prove via Courant–Fischer: $x^\top SAS^\top x=y^\top Ay$ with $y=S^\top x$ and $\sigma_n^2\|x\|^2\le\|y\|^2\le\sigma_1^2\|x\|^2$.

results.title: Simultaneous diagonalisation of a definite pair by congruence
results.informal: If $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ is symmetric positive definite and $B$ symmetric, there is a nonsingular $S$ with $A=SS^\top$ and $B=S\Lambda S^\top$, $\Lambda$ real diagonal whose entries are the eigenvalues of $A^{-1}B$ (and $\Lambda$ has the inertia of $B$). Consequently $A^{-1}B$ (and $AB$) is diagonalisable with real eigenvalues, nonnegative if $B\succeq0$. More generally (Thm 4.5.17) for invertible symmetric $A$, $A,B$ are simultaneously congruent to real diagonals iff $A^{-1}B$ is diagonalisable with real spectrum. A PSD–PSD version holds with $A=S(I_r\oplus0)S^\top$.
results.notes: Consumers: spectrum of the preconditioned operator $P^{-1}A$ in `preconditioned-cg` and `nystrom-pcg`, generalized eigenproblems, Loewner-sandwich arguments (`loewner-relative-spectrum`). Prove: Cholesky $A=LL^\top$, then diagonalise $L^{-1}BL^{-\top}$.

results.title: Geršgorin refinements and diagonal dominance
results.informal: Let $R_i=\sum_{j\ne i}|a_{ij}|$, $C_j=\sum_{i\ne j}|a_{ij}|$. (i) A union of $k$ Geršgorin discs disjoint from the remaining $n-k$ contains exactly $k$ eigenvalues; the column discs work too. (ii) $\rho(A)\le\min\{\max_i\sum_j|a_{ij}|,\max_j\sum_i|a_{ij}|\}$, and with positive weights $\rho(A)\le\max_ip_i^{-1}\sum_jp_j|a_{ij}|$. (iii) If $A$ is strictly diagonally dominant ($|a_{ii}|>R_i$) with positive diagonal, every eigenvalue has positive real part; if moreover $A$ is symmetric it is positive definite. (iv) Taussky: an irreducibly diagonally dominant matrix is nonsingular (and PD if symmetric with positive diagonal).
hypotheses: $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$ (real symmetric for the PD conclusions)
results.conclusion: eigenvalue counts in isolated disc unions; row/column-sum spectral radius bounds; diagonal dominance ⇒ Re λ > 0 / PD

mathlib_prereqs.note: Defined for nonnegative matrices; irreducibility of a general matrix via its pattern is not in Mathlib.

results.notes: Consumers: positive definiteness of diagonally dominant matrices (graph Laplacians plus shifts, kernel matrices with a nugget, preconditioners), spectral-radius bounds for Jacobi-type iterations (`richardson-iteration`), eigenvalue localisation for nearly diagonal matrices (diagonal estimation, `diagonal-estimator`). Do (ii)–(iii) first (difficulty 1–2); the counting part needs continuity of eigenvalues (assume or prove via the argument principle); Taussky later.

results.title: Bauer–Fike theorem and residual bounds for diagonalisable matrices
results.informal: Let $A=V\Lambda V^{-1}$ be diagonalisable and $E$ arbitrary. Every eigenvalue $\hat\lambda$ of $A+E$ satisfies $\min_i|\hat\lambda-\lambda_i|\le\kappa(V)\,|||E|||$ for any matrix norm induced by an absolute vector norm (e.g. $\|\cdot\|_1,\|\cdot\|_2,\|\cdot\|_\infty$), with $\kappa(V)=|||V|||\,|||V^{-1}|||$. If $A$ is normal, $\min_i|\hat\lambda-\lambda_i|\le\|E\|_2$. Residual form: for $\hat x\ne0$ and $r=A\hat x-\hat\lambda\hat x$, $\min_i|\hat\lambda-\lambda_i|\le\kappa(V)\|r\|/\|\hat x\|$ (and $\le\|r\|_2/\|\hat x\|_2$ for normal $A$).
hypotheses: norm induced by an absolute vector norm
results.notes: Consumers: `gmres-diagonalizable` (the $\kappa(V)$ factor), `eigenvalue-residual-bounds` (normal case generalises its part (a)), eigenvalue sensitivity in `qr-algorithm-convergence`. Prove: if $\hat\lambda\notin\sigma(A)$ then $I+(\Lambda-\hat\lambda)^{-1}V^{-1}EV$ is singular, so $1\le\|(\Lambda-\hat\lambda)^{-1}\|\kappa(V)\|E\|$; spectral-norm case first (difficulty 2).

results.title: Hoffman–Wielandt inequality for normal matrices
results.informal: If $A$ and $A+E$ are normal with eigenvalues $\lambda_i$ and $\hat\lambda_i$, there is a permutation $\sigma$ with $\sum_i|\hat\lambda_{\sigma(i)}-\lambda_i|^2\le\|E\|_F^2$.
results.notes: The symmetric case is already in candidate `eigenvalue-perturbation-symmetric` (Cor 6.3.8); this entry is the normal-matrix generality. Proof: unitary diagonalisations turn $\|E\|_F^2$ into a linear function of the doubly stochastic matrix $[|u_{ij}|^2]$, minimised at a permutation (Birkhoff).

results.title: First-order perturbation of a simple eigenvalue
results.informal: Let $\lambda$ be a simple eigenvalue of $A$ with right and left eigenvectors $x,y$. Then $y^*x\ne0$, $A$ is similar to $\lambda\oplus A_1$ with $\lambda\notin\sigma(A_1)$, and for every $E$ there is a unique eigenvalue $\lambda(t)$ of $A+tE$ near $\lambda$ for small $|t|$, continuous and differentiable at $0$ with $\lambda'(0)=y^*Ex/y^*x$. For symmetric $A$ with unit eigenvector $x$: $\lambda'(0)=x^\top Ex$.
hypotheses: $\lambda$ an algebraically simple eigenvalue of $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$

mathlib_prereqs.note: Not packaged in Mathlib for matrix eigenvalues.

results.notes: Consumers: derivative of $\lambda_{\max}$ (matrix calculus for spectral functions), eigenvalue condition numbers $1/|y^*x|$, sensitivity of Ritz values. Assume is acceptable.

results.title: Sylvester's criterion for positive (semi)definiteness
results.informal: For symmetric $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$: $A\succ0$ iff all leading principal minors $\det A_{[1..k]}$ are positive (equivalently all trailing ones); $A\succeq0$ iff all principal minors (not just leading) are nonnegative; if the first $n-1$ leading minors are positive and $\det A\ge0$ then $A\succeq0$. Also: $A\succeq0$ iff the nonzero coefficients of its characteristic polynomial strictly alternate in sign.
results.notes: Consumers: existence of LU/Cholesky without pivoting for SPD matrices (`lu-decomposition`, `cholesky-algorithm`), positivity of pivots in `rpcholesky` and `partial-cholesky-nystrom`, principal-minor arguments in `volume-sampling`. Prove the PD case by induction with `posDef_iff_pivotSchur` and `det_eq_mul_det_pivotSchur`; PSD case via $A+\varepsilon I$.

results.title: Matrices with positive (semi)definite Hermitian part
results.informal: Let $A=H+iK$ with $H,K$ Hermitian. If $H\succeq0$ then $\ker A\subseteq\ker H$, $\operatorname{rank}H\le\operatorname{rank}A$, and $A$ has the row/column inclusion property when the ranks agree (always when $H\succ0$). If $H\succ0$: $\det H\le|\det A|$ (Ostrowski–Taussky, equality iff $K=0$), $\det H+|\det K|\le|\det A|$ for $n\ge2$, and $(\det H)^{2/n}+|\det K|^{2/n}\le|\det A|^{2/n}$ (Fan).
results.conclusion: null-space/rank relations; determinant lower bounds for $|\det A|$
results.notes: Consumers: positive-real (accretive) matrices in `gmres-elman` and `gmres-bgt`, field-of-values arguments. Low priority; the rank/null-space facts are routine, the determinant inequalities follow from simultaneous diagonalisation of $(H,K)$.

results.title: Interlacing of singular values under row or column deletion
results.informal: If $\hat A$ is obtained from $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ by deleting one row or one column, then with $q=\min(m,n)$ and $\hat\sigma_q:=0$ when the deletion lowers the smaller dimension: $\sigma_1(A)\ge\hat\sigma_1\ge\sigma_2(A)\ge\hat\sigma_2\ge\dots\ge\sigma_q(A)\ge\hat\sigma_q$. Iterating: for a $p\times r$ submatrix $A_{IJ}$, $\sigma_{i+(m-p)+(n-r)}(A)\le\sigma_i(A_{IJ})\le\sigma_i(A)$.
hypotheses: $\hat A$: one row or column deleted (or a general submatrix)
results.notes: Consumers: column subset selection and CUR (`volume-sampling`, `interpolative-decomposition`, `rank-revealing-qr`: $\sigma_i(A_{:,S})\le\sigma_i(A)$), sketch-and-solve with row sampling (`leverage-sampling-ose`), Nyström blocks. Prove: $\hat A^\top\hat A$ (column deletion) is a principal submatrix of $A^\top A$, or $\hat A^\top\hat A=A^\top A-aa^\top$ (row deletion); apply `cauchy-interlacing` / `low-rank-update-interlacing` and `sq_singularValues_eq_eigenvalues₀`.

results.title: Equal Gram matrices differ by an isometry
aliases: A^T A = B^T B iff B = V A
results.informal: For $A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}$ and $B\in\mathbb R^{q\times n}$ with $p\le q$: $A^\top A=B^\top B$ iff $B=VA$ for some $V\in\mathbb R^{q\times p}$ with orthonormal columns.
results.conclusion: $A^\top A=B^\top B\iff\exists V,\ V^\top V=I_p,\ B=VA$
results.notes: Consumers: uniqueness of Gram/Cholesky-type factors up to rotation (`nystrom-structural`, `exists_eq_transpose_mul_of_posSemidef` users), sketch equivalences where only $A^\top S^\top SA$ matters, `polar-decomposition` uniqueness. Prove via SVD of $A$ and $B$.

results.title: Polar decomposition: existence and uniqueness
results.informal: Every $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ with $m\ge n$ factors as $A=UQ$ with $Q=(A^\top A)^{1/2}\succeq0$ uniquely determined and $U\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ with orthonormal columns, unique iff $\operatorname{rank}A=n$ (then $U=A(A^\top A)^{-1/2}$); for $m\le n$, $A=PU$ with $P=(AA^\top)^{1/2}$; for square $A$, $A=PU=UQ$ with $U$ orthogonal. $U$ is the nearest matrix with orthonormal columns to $A$ in every unitarily invariant norm.
results.conclusion: $A=UQ$, $Q=(A^\top A)^{1/2}$, $U^\top U=I$; uniqueness under full rank

mathlib_prereqs.note: Matrix square root via the continuous functional calculus.

results.notes: NLAlib already has the full-column-rank real case as `polarFrame` (`hasOrthonormalCols_polarFrame`, `polarFrame_mul_transpose_mul_eq`); this entry adds the rank-deficient and square cases and uniqueness. Consumers: `orthogonal-procrustes`, `principal-angles-def` (polar factor of $Q^\top\hat Q$), orthonormalisation of sketches in `rsvd-expected-error`/`subspace-iteration-def`, `haar-orthogonal`. Prove from the SVD.

results.title: Orthogonal Procrustes and nearest scaled orthogonal matrix
results.informal: For $A,B\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$: $\min_{U\in O(m)}\|A-UB\|_F^2=\|A\|_F^2-2\sum_i\sigma_i(AB^\top)+\|B\|_F^2$, attained at the orthogonal polar factor of $AB^\top$; $\min_{U,T\text{ orth.}}\|A-UBT\|_F^2=\sum_i(\sigma_i(A)-\sigma_i(B))^2$; the best $cU$ approximation of square $A$ is $(\tfrac1n\operatorname{tr}P)U_0$ for $A=PU_0$. Equality $\|A-B\|_F^2=\sum_i(\sigma_i(A)-\sigma_i(B))^2$ holds iff $\operatorname{tr}AB^\top=\sum\sigma_i(A)\sigma_i(B)$, and then $AB^\top,B^\top A\succeq0$.
results.conclusion: closed-form minima and minimisers of the Procrustes problems; equality case of von Neumann/Mirsky
results.notes: Consumers: aligning subspace bases before comparing them (`principal-angles-def`, `davis-kahan-sin-theta`, `wedin-sin-theta` applications), comparing sketches up to rotation. Prove from von Neumann (`frobInner_le_sum_singularValues_mul`) plus attainment at the polar factor.

results.title: Kantorovich and Wielandt inequalities
aliases: angle bound for positive definite forms
results.informal: Let $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric positive definite with extreme eigenvalues $\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max}$ and $\kappa=\lambda_{\max}/\lambda_{\min}$. Kantorovich: $(x^\top Ax)(x^\top A^{-1}x)\le\frac{(\lambda_{\min}+\lambda_{\max})^2}{4\lambda_{\min}\lambda_{\max}}\|x\|^4=\tfrac14(\kappa^{1/2}+\kappa^{-1/2})^2\|x\|^4$. Wielandt: for orthogonal $x,y$, $(x^\top Ay)^2\le\big(\frac{\lambda_{\max}-\lambda_{\min}}{\lambda_{\max}+\lambda_{\min}}\big)^2(x^\top Ax)(y^\top Ay)$. The two inequalities are equivalent.
results.notes: Consumers: steepest-descent rate $\big(\frac{\kappa-1}{\kappa+1}\big)^2$ (contrast with `cg-convergence`), Wielandt angle bounds for preconditioned or sketched inner products (`sketch-and-precondition`, `ose-def`: angle distortion), randomized Kaczmarz/coordinate descent variants. Prove Kantorovich from $(\lambda_{\max}I-A)(A-\lambda_{\min}I)A^{-1}\succeq0$ as in the book; Wielandt from Kantorovich on a $2\times2$ compression.

results.title: Self-duality of the PSD cone (Fejér–Moutard)
results.informal: A symmetric $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ is positive semidefinite iff $\operatorname{tr}(AB)=\sum_{ij}a_{ij}b_{ij}\ge0$ for every positive semidefinite $B$. In particular $\operatorname{tr}(AB)\ge0$ for $A,B\succeq0$, with equality iff $AB=0$; and $\operatorname{tr}(AB)\le\operatorname{tr}(AC)$ when $A\succeq0$ and $B\preceq C$.
results.notes: Consumers: ubiquitous trace manipulations — matrix Laplace/Chernoff bounds (`matrix-laplace`, `matrix-chernoff`), variance formulas in `hutchinson-variance`, monotonicity $\operatorname{tr}(AB)\le\operatorname{tr}(AC)$ in Nyström and Hutch++ proofs, `generalized-schur-complement-psd`. Prove: forward via $\operatorname{tr}(AB)=\operatorname{tr}(B^{1/2}AB^{1/2})$; converse with $B=xx^\top$.

results.title: Schur (Hadamard) product inequalities
results.informal: For PSD $A,B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$: if $A\succ0$ and $B$ has positive diagonal then $A\circ B\succ0$; Hadamard powers $A^{\circ k}$ and $[f(a_{ij})]$ for $f$ with nonnegative Taylor coefficients (radius $>\max|a_{ij}|$) are PSD, $[e^{a_{ij}}]\succeq0$ (PD iff no two rows of $A$ coincide); Oppenheim: $\det(A\circ B)\ge\max\{\det A\prod b_{ii},\det B\prod a_{ii}\}$; for $A,B\succ0$: $A^{-1}\circ B^{-1}\succeq(A\circ B)^{-1}$, $A\circ A^{-1}\succeq I$, and $\lambda_{\min}(A\circ B)\ge\max\{\lambda_{\min}(AB),\lambda_{\min}(AB^\top)\}$; Hadamard products preserve the dominance $x^*Ax\ge|x^*Bx|$.
results.conclusion: the listed Loewner, determinant and eigenvalue inequalities for $A\circ B$

mathlib_prereqs.note: $A\circ B$ is a principal submatrix of $A\otimes B$.

results.notes: Consumers: positive definiteness of kernel matrices built entrywise (Gaussian/exponential kernels for Nyström, `rpcholesky` on kernel matrices), Rademacher/diagonal estimator variance terms involving $A\circ A$ (`diagonal-estimator`, `hutchinson-variance`), Oppenheim for determinantal sampling. Low priority; assume where convenient.

results.title: Concavity of log det, Minkowski determinant inequality and convexity of tr A⁻¹
results.informal: On symmetric positive definite matrices: $A\mapsto\log\det A$ is strictly concave, i.e. $\det(\alpha A+(1-\alpha)B)\ge(\det A)^\alpha(\det B)^{1-\alpha}$ for $0<\alpha<1$ with equality iff $A=B$; $A\mapsto(\det A)^{1/n}$ is concave (Minkowski: $(\det(A+B))^{1/n}\ge(\det A)^{1/n}+(\det B)^{1/n}$, equality iff $A=cB$); and $A\mapsto\operatorname{tr}A^{-1}$ is strictly convex.
results.conclusion: the three concavity/convexity statements with equality cases
results.notes: Consumers: log-determinant estimation by SLQ (`slq-error`: concavity gives Jensen bounds), `volume-sampling` and determinantal sampling, D-/A-optimal design objectives, Jensen steps for inverse Wishart traces (`inverse-wishart-mean`: convexity of $\operatorname{tr}A^{-1}$). Prove by simultaneous diagonalisation reducing to scalar AM–GM / convexity of $1/x$; NLAlib’s operator concavity of log (`operator-monotone-convex`) gives log det concavity directly via $\log\det=\operatorname{tr}\log$.

results.title: Loewner order versus the spectrum of A⁻¹B, and monotone spectral functions
results.informal: Let $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric positive definite and $B$ symmetric. Then $aA\preceq B\preceq bA$ iff every eigenvalue of $A^{-1}B$ lies in $[a,b]$; for $B\succeq0$, $A\succeq B$ iff $\rho(A^{-1}B)\le1$ iff $B=A^{1/2}XA^{1/2}$ with $0\preceq X\preceq I$, and $A^2\succeq B^2$ iff $\|A^{-1}B\|\le1$. If $A\succeq B\succeq0$: $\det A\ge\det B$, $\operatorname{tr}A\ge\operatorname{tr}B$ with equality iff $A=B$, $\lambda_i(A)\ge\lambda_i(B)$, and $B^{-1}\succeq A^{-1}$, $A^{1/2}\succeq B^{1/2}$ when defined.
results.conclusion: equivalence of the Loewner sandwich with the relative spectrum; monotonicity of det, trace, eigenvalues, inverse and square root
results.notes: Consumers: `preconditioned-cg` (hypothesis $aP\preceq A\preceq bP$ ⇔ $\sigma(P^{-1}A)\subseteq[a,b]$, giving the condition number $b/a$), `nystrom-pcg`, `ose-def` (subspace embedding as a Loewner sandwich of Gram matrices), `sketch-and-precondition`; determinant monotonicity for `volume-sampling`. Prove via `simultaneous-diagonalization-congruence` or directly with $A^{-1/2}BA^{-1/2}$; eigenvalue and trace parts are already in NLAlib.

results.title: PSD block matrices: contractions, Schur complements and inverse principal submatrices
results.informal: For $X\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}$: $\begin{bmatrix}I&X\\X^\top&I\end{bmatrix}\succeq0$ ($\succ0$) iff $\|X\|\le1$ ($<1$). For $H=\begin{bmatrix}A&B\\B^\top&C\end{bmatrix}$ with $A,C\succeq0$, TFAE: $H\succeq0$; $(x^\top Ax)(y^\top Cy)\ge(x^\top By)^2$ for all $x,y$; $x^\top Ax+y^\top Cy\ge2|x^\top By|$; $B=A^{1/2}XC^{1/2}$ with $\|X\|\le1$; if $A,C\succ0$ also $\rho(B^\top A^{-1}BC^{-1})\le1$ (strict versions characterise $H\succ0$, equivalently $A\succ0$ and $C-B^\top A^{-1}B\succ0$). For $A,B\succeq0$: $A\succeq B$ iff $\begin{bmatrix}A&B\\B&A\end{bmatrix}\succeq0$. For $H\succ0$ and an index set $\alpha$: $(H^{-1})_{\alpha\alpha}\succeq(H_{\alpha\alpha})^{-1}$; $\begin{bmatrix}A&X\\X^\top&X^\top A^{-1}X\end{bmatrix}\succeq0$ for $A\succ0$.
results.conclusion: the listed equivalences and Loewner inequalities
results.notes: Consumers: Cauchy–Schwarz for PSD bilinear forms in approximate-matrix-multiplication and subspace-embedding proofs (`amm-ose`, `ose-def`), Nyström error via Schur complements (`nystrom-structural`, `generalized-schur-complement-psd`), inverse-diagonal lower bounds $(A^{-1})_{ii}\ge1/a_{ii}$ for diagonal estimation of $A^{-1}$ (`diagonal-estimator`), Hermitian dilation arguments. Prove from `posSemidef_fromBlocks_iff` (currently assumed) and the square root.

results.title: Hadamard, Fischer, Koteljanskiĭ and Szász determinant inequalities
results.informal: For symmetric positive definite $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$: $\det A\le\prod_ia_{ii}$ with equality iff $A$ is diagonal (Hadamard), hence $|\det B|\le\prod_j\|b_j\|_2$ for any square $B$ with columns $b_j$ (equality iff orthogonal columns or a zero column); $\det\begin{bmatrix}A_{11}&A_{12}\\A_{21}&A_{22}\end{bmatrix}\le\det A_{11}\det A_{22}$ (Fischer); $\det A_{\alpha\cup\beta}\det A_{\alpha\cap\beta}\le\det A_\alpha\det A_\beta$ (Koteljanskiĭ); and the normalised products $P_k^{1/\binom{n-1}{k-1}}$ of $k\times k$ principal minors decrease in $k$ (Szász).
results.conclusion: the listed determinant inequalities with equality cases
results.notes: Consumers: `volume-sampling` and column subset selection (Gram determinants bounded by products of column norms; NLAlib already has the base-times-height identity `det_gram_fromCols_eq_mul_frobSq_sub_projector`), `rpcholesky` / `partial-cholesky-nystrom` (determinants of pivot blocks), determinant bounds for random matrices. Prove Hadamard from Cholesky ($\det A=\prod L_{ii}^2$, `IsCholesky.det_eq_prod_sq`, with $L_{ii}^2\le a_{ii}$) or QR ($|\det B|=\prod|R_{ii}|\le\prod\|b_j\|$); Fischer from the Schur complement $A_{22}-A_{21}A_{11}^{-1}A_{12}\preceq A_{22}$; Koteljanskiĭ and Szász later.
